Saturday Preview: Can Mr Brightside make history in Makybe Diva Stakes?

Bjorn Baker-trained pair of Group 1 winners Overpass and Caballus showed they are on track for their spring targets with a one-two at the trials at Randwick on Friday. They’ll both resume on Everest day. Napoleonic made his trial win look easy, while Farnicle was strong late when second in his trial. Chris Waller scratched Buckaroo and Birdman from the G1 Makybe Diva Stakes and they had a hit out at Flemington instead. (Baker's G1 Winners Impress in Randwick Trials)
Bjorn Baker heads into the new season with a strong team, featuring established stars, exciting 3-year-old sprinters and a promising crop of 2-year-olds about to potentially make their mark.

Cambridge Stud is backing its New Zealand stallion roster with depth at home, while sending select Group 1 mares across the Tasman, with new recruit Charyn attracting some of the farm’s best mares this season.

Arrowfield Stud's Japanese shuttle Maurice has faced more than the usual pressures in the early years of a stallion's career. Locked out of Australia in his fourth season with only a small crop of foals in his third, his turnaround in fortunes has been quite remarkable.

Warnie produced a brilliant performance to claim the delayed G3 Chautauqua Stakes at Sandown, before 3-year-olds Tales Of Time and Regal Ambition impressed at the same venue, while Wonka saluted on the Kensington on Wednesday in impressive style.

Time in racing is not the same everywhere. Some jurisdictions measure from when the gates open; others from a point several metres in front of the gates. But when Ka Ying Rising burned up the Sha Tin track on Sunday night, he set a sensational time from a standing start that is the (adjusted) fastest 1200 metres of all time. (Ka Ying Rising Posts Adjusted Fastest 1200m of All Time)

Star Thoroughbreds were thrilled with the $250,000 they received for stakes placed Chatterley. (Bellatrix Star Tops Inglis Digital Sale at $900,000)
